newsitem.title: UK: Rifkind says UK will work to change EU directive.
newsitem.headline: Rifkind says UK will work to change EU directive.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on Tuesday the government would work to change the European Court of Justice ruling imposing maximum working hours on the UK.
Speaking to reporters on the way into the Confederation of British Industry's annual conference, Rifkind said, "we'll obey the law and we'll work to change the law."
He added that the imposition of uniform rules across the whole of Europe was "absurd" and said employers and employees should be free to work out their own arrangements.
In a speech to the conference, Rifkind said the government shared the CBI's "disappointment" over the European Court ruling.

He said the ruling was "legally correct but goes against the spirit of what was negotiated in the Maastricht Treaty", and he confirmed the government would use the EU inter-governmental conference (IGC) to pursue the dispute.

But Rifkind made clear the government's respect for the European Court of Justice, saying the rules of the Single Market had to be respected, and they could only be enforced by the European Commission and the European Court of Justice.
